newsitem.title: USA: Quaker Oats recalls FrescAvena drink mix.
newsitem.headline: Quaker Oats recalls FrescAvena drink mix.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said on Friday that it is recalling 127 cases of its cinnamon-flavored FrescAvena beverage mix distributed in the metropolitan New York/New Jersey area.
Foreign objects, including glass fragments, were found in packages of the drink mix sold at a ShopRite supermarket in Passaic, New Jersey.
The product code of the recalled product is 10G6C7.
FrescAvena, a flavored mix added to milk, is manufactured by a Quaker subsidiary's plants in Venezuela and Colombia. The recalled product was made in the Venezuela facility.
Although primarily sold in Latin America, Quaker said FrescAvena is imported for sale in certain U.S. regions.

A spokesman for the company said a consumer called Thursday after giving the drink to his young son. The supermarket pulled the mix from its shelves, and a Quaker representative examined the mix and found glass fragments.

"The consumer who called us had given some of the product to his young son," said Quaker spokesman Ronald Bottrell. "He did take the boy into the hospital for examination but it appears the boy is fine."

Bottrell said this is Quaker's first complaint of contamination in FrescAvena, and at this point the cause of the contamination is unknown. The company said it will investigate both in the United States and Venezuela to determine the source.
"We're certainly doing spot checks of other lots," Bottrell said. "We're obviously going to be doing a very thorough investigation."
The store where the contaminated product was bought had sold about 11 canisters of the drink mix, Bottrell said. Each canister makes about 20 servings.
For more information on the FrescAvena recall, consumers can call 1-800-252-1109.
